episode_title: Episode 520: November Retinal Physician Review Including How Retina Trials Are Designed, Building a Clinical Trial Program, Solo Retina Practice, Operating Room Access

real_qa.q: What is the difference between superiority trials and non-inferiority trials in wet AMD drug development?
real_qa.r: A superiority trial asks whether you outperformed the control arm on a pre-specified endpoint. Non-inferiority is almost like a double negative—it supports the conclusion that you are not worse than the comparator by more than a pre-specified margin. For wet AMD, non-inferiority has been defined as being up to four and a half ETDRS letters worse than ranibizumab or aflibercept two milligram and still considered non-inferior.
real_qa.requete: superiority vs non-inferiority trials wet AMD

real_qa.q: Can a single clinical trial support FDA approval for a new wet AMD drug instead of requiring two trials?
real_qa.r: Yes, according to 2026 FDA guidance, there can be circumstances in which one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation can satisfy the evidence standard. However, the trial must have a p-value less than 0.001 and cannot be borderline. Historically, in 1995-1997, 80.6% of drugs were approved based on two trials, but that dropped to 52.8% in 2015-2017, showing this trend is occurring across medicine.
real_qa.requete: single trial FDA approval wet AMD 2026

real_qa.q: What is a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) in FDA drug approval for retinal trials?
real_qa.r: An SPA is a special protocol assessment that essentially says if you are aligned with FDA standards, it reduces regulatory risks and increases your chances of a positive role, assuming you meet the criteria. It allows for feedback from the FDA during the trial design phase before you submit your NDA, though it does not guarantee approval. The FDA released guidance in February 2023 specifying that trials should have at least 400 patients receiving the experimental drug for safety and at least 300 followed through nine months prior to submitting the NDA.
real_qa.requete: Special Protocol Assessment SPA FDA retinal trials

real_qa.q: Why is there overlap between retinal researchers, drug company consultants, and medical journal editors in ophthalmology?
real_qa.r: The retina field is a small field to begin with, yet has a lot of research, creating natural overlap in the roles people carry. As Dr. Schreeder notes, there is not like a million people out there who know about surgical retina trials or trial design, so the same people cycle through academic positions, company consulting, editorial roles, and speaking engagements. While this creates potential conflicts of interest, it reflects the reality that only a limited number of specialists possess the expertise to educate on these complex topics.

real_qa.q: What was the CAT trial and why was it significant for understanding non-inferiority in retinal medicine?
real_qa.r: The CAT trial compared ranibizumab to bevacizumab in either monthly or as-needed dosing with four arms. It was very popular as a teaching topic because people were confused when it came out—they were not used to the non-inferiority discussion. The trial showed there was not a non-inferiority standard because the lower bound of the confidence interval crossed the non-inferiority margin for monthly versus as-needed comparisons.
